scope: First published attempt; exact per-mesh hashes retained. Later native exports must be rebound after publication. These are geometry explanations, not print release.

classified.reason: [step] The standing Z-seam rail-channel walls at nominal |X|103.75 lie 0.75 mm inward from the |X|104.5 flank face. `_rail_channel_span` derives them from the rail head and 0.25 mm running clearance. The common floor and continuous exterior wall back the channel; this offset is the rail's sliding passage.

[sliver] The aft flavour-valve tray's end lands expose its solid plate-to-flank root. The plate is 9.2 mm deep at Y172.09..181.29 and finishes on the flank's 45-degree bedding plane. The 0.5 mm exposed height is the end of that intersection, backed by the complete plate depth and the adjoining wall. The lower band stays inset from the lip; each wall root begins at Z177.9.

[sliver] These are the exposed ends of the carrier floor between its fore plane at Y93.836 and the tee wells' front plane at Y94.040. The floor runs from Z160 to Z166.924. Native probes verify a continuous 9.998 mm-wide section extending inboard from these faces; the 0.204 mm reading is the exposed Y length of the floor end, not its material thickness. See postpublish-front-top-stock-check.json.

[sliver] The outer tee well ends at |X|96.9297 and the 9 mm flank begins at |X|98.5. The exposed top and aft faces of their joined guide land are 1.5703 mm across. The land runs from the recess roof at Z229.619 to the fixed-body top at Z235.925 and joins the flank along its length. Native probes retain a complete 5.98 mm-wide wall-root block behind that land on both sides; its exposed face width is not a separate thin wall. See postpublish-front-top-stock-check.json.

[ceiling] The front Z-slide heads' square catches stand at z=160.00 + 8.70 + 0.25 running clearance + 0.25 supported-face allowance = 169.20. Each overlaps the top's full-section foot and retains at least 3 mm of head stock. Lifting the seated top lands the flat foot on this face along the rail; its flat bearing resists lift without camming the seam open. The arm returns to the wall on its 45-degree under-flare, and slicer support carries the catch underside. The groove under the catch is open air from the arm's sliding face out past the exterior plane, so that support stands on the outside of the flank with a face exposed down the whole run; it comes off in one piece without reaching into the cavity.
